## Introduction

This report analyzes the results of the LIONESS algorithm applied to the dataset, specifically focusing on interactions that have been validated by the STRING database.

## Methodology

The LIONESS algorithm was used to estimate sample-specific networks. The following thresholds and metrics were applied in the analysis pipeline (see `analysis/lioness.R`):

*   **Correlation Threshold:** Edges were retained if their weight exceeded the Mean + 2 * Standard Deviation of the edge weights across all samples.
*   **Significance Threshold:** Differential connectivity was assessed using a t-test between conditions. P-values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure. Edges with an adjusted p-value < 0.05 were considered significant.
*   **STRING Validation:** Significant edges were further filtered to include only those with known interactions in the STRING database (see `analysis/lioness_filter_string.R`).

## Results

### Top 10 Genes by Degree

The following table shows the top 10 genes with the highest degree (number of connections) in the STRING-filtered LIONESS network.

````{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(igraph)
library(easylayout)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

# Load the filtered edges
# Assumes the report is rendered from the 'analysis' directory
edges <- read_csv("../results/lioness_significant_edges_string.csv")

# Calculate degree
# Combine gene1 and gene2 to get all gene occurrences
all_genes <- c(edges$gene1, edges$gene2)
degree_counts <- table(all_genes)

# Map ENSEMBL IDs to SYMBOLs
ensembl_ids <- names(degree_counts)
symbols <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, 
                                 keys = ensembl_ids, 
                                 column = "SYMBOL", 
                                 keytype = "ENSEMBL", 
                                 multiVals = "first")

# Replace NAs with the original ENSEMBL IDs just in case they are not found
symbols[is.na(symbols)] <- ensembl_ids[is.na(symbols)]

# Create a data frame for the table
degree_df <- data.frame(
  Gene = unname(symbols),
  Degree = as.integer(degree_counts)
)

# Sort by degree (descending) and take top 10
top_10_genes <- degree_df %>%
  arrange(desc(Degree)) %>%
  head(10)

# Display table
kable(top_10_genes, caption = "Top 10 Genes by Degree")
````
